pages.title: About Us — Kelwin

pages.oneLine: The firm behind the signature: the person who signed the letter, the five rules he runs every engagement by, and the week an engagement runs on — then the first step.
pages.question: Who is actually behind this, can I trust them with my revenue system, and how would they work with us?

It designs, installs and runs revenue systems that its clients keep. It stays small, so the person who diagnoses your system is the person who answers your email.” Facts: Founded · 2026 — deliberately late to the category [K letter] · Led by · Rameez, Founder · Lead Narrative Architect [K] (FC) · Starts with · The System Audit ↗ (quiet link to /audit).

sections.content: Label “■ What we believe” · h3 [N] “The rules every engagement is built on.” 01 Diagnosis before prescription [K] — “No engagement starts without the audit's readout — building before diagnosing sells the same fix to every different problem.” [K] · Binds at Diagnose. 02 Assets first — then the retainer [K] — “Everything we install is documented in your language and lives in your stack. The operating retainer compounds a system you own — it never becomes the thing you rent.” [K, approved service model] · Binds at Handover, Calibrate. 03 Clarity is infrastructure [K] — [R] “Most pipeline problems are narrative problems in disguise. We write the language down before we build anything that carries it.” · Architect. 04 Learning is the asset [R, was “Compounding beats resetting”] — [R] “What an engagement learns is written into the system, so next quarter starts where this one ended.” · Calibrate. 05 The exit test [K] — “If it stops working the day we leave, we built it wrong. Every engagement is designed backwards from this sentence.” [K] · Handover.

pages.title: <Layer> — Kelwin

pages.question: What exactly would you build in this layer, what would I hold, and who runs it after?
pages.templateRules: Five slots: head → services → specimen (paper) → runs → door. Slot ORDER and every layout differ per page (see instances[].order). Facts ledger keeps the approved X keys: Engagement · Scoped at the readout (FS) · Output · <two homepage assets> — yours (FS) · Starts with · The System Audit ↗ [K]. Four services per layer named exactly as the nav's 0n.1–0n.4, each “Ships” an artifact that rolls up into one of two assets. Removed everywhere: install durations, Phase I/II, 3×2 stat cards, defensive stamps, “yours when we leave”, any claim the audit “instruments”. ≤2 readings per page, none of the homepage's four.

SpecimenTag “Specimen · illustrative rules. Every install writes its own from the ICP & Signal Map.”

sections.content: Sections (format [N], one “Example” each) (FC structure): 01 The constraint, named — “One sentence: the layer holding revenue back, and the evidence for it.” Example “The committee can't repeat what you do in one sentence, so deals stall at the second meeting.” · 02 Narrative readout — “How your market repeats you today, in buyers' words, across site, deck, sequences and calls.” Example: three one-line descriptions of the company (founder, seller, engineer) that don't match · 03 Channel orchestration map — “Every channel you run, what triggers each touch, and where demand leaks.” Example: a mini TRACE with two leaks marked · 04 Intelligence gap report — “What your GTM decisions rest on today, and what nobody is measuring.” Example: Known · Not written down · Not measured · 05 Rebuild sequence — “The order to fix things in, and what each step needs. Yours either way.” Example: four quarter columns · 06 Next step — “If installation makes sense, we scope it there. If not, the plan is still yours.” [K].

shared.name: SectionHead
shared.spec: Label row (■ label, no meta) → one-line h3 → optional lede. At most two two-voice statements per page (the h1 plus one).

shared.name: Door (five variants)
shared.spec: D1 decision band: label + one display sentence (32–42px) naming what the audit returns for this subject (documented scope only) + red “Request a System Audit” → /audit + .ac-link “Talk to the team” → /contact + a small page object + one onward link. D2 statement: 64px two-voice + lede + doors. D3 gate close: honest list left, gate line + doors right. SC split close: two things side by side. QC quiet close: quiet links only, no red. The red plane stays homepage-only.

shared.name: SiblingStrip
shared.spec: The three capability glyphs (CONTOUR · TRACE · ORBIT) in a row, “You are here” on the current one, each other one a link with its relation verb (Carried by / Measured by / Carries / Read by / Feeds / Reads).

shared.name: SpecimenTag
shared.spec: A mono “Specimen” chip (≥11px) + one support line ≥13.5px naming what is illustrative (“… No client data.”). Every illustrative artifact carries one, which keeps Terms L·03 true.

shared.name: Readings
shared.spec: ≤2 per page, none of the homepage's four. Number + unit in words + source · year + link (new tab, visually hidden “opens in a new tab”), hedged as the source hedges it. Kept: 6–10 and 81%→31% (Narrative), 1 in 6 and 28% (Infrastructure), 45% (Intelligence). Re-verify every link before launch.

shared.name: MailtoConfirm
shared.spec: After a mailto submit: a confirmation state (“Your mail app should have opened … Nothing is sent until you press send.”) + the address with a Copy button, for visitors with no mail client. No network call (Privacy coupling).

founderQuestions: Q1 · Who is Kelwin today (D11)? You alone, or other senior people? Interior pages say “Rameez” / “the founder” and /about says “One architect today”; the approved homepage CTA and FAQ say “the founding team” — keep or change? One line of background under your name, or none? Confirm “Founder · Lead Narrative Architect” and “Based · London”. No portrait (rule 6) unless you grant one exception. Is the next seat only a Systems Engineer?

Q2 · Track record: have any audits or installs run yet, even unpublishable ones? If not, the field notes' “we audit / we've run / we see” lines become your own first-person observation, and the 17% note's “predictor of close” finding is cut (or kept as a stated hypothesis) — which?

Q3 · The rest of D8 and replies: confirm the readout's four parts (narrative readout, channel orchestration map, intelligence gap report, sequenced rebuild plan) and whether there is a 60-minute readout call — /audit and the /reports specimen are built on them. Reply times: one working day for audit bookings, two for everything else? Bench-list mail to audit@ or a careers address?

Q4 · The Lab: R&D that sharpens the installs (default) or a product heading to a standalone console? Which instruments exist today and at which stage (concept / prototype / used on engagements / released)? Install clients first? Does the advisory work fund it? Is the Entropy Index benchmark still on for Q4 2026? Keep The Lab top-level in the nav (default), or under The Firm as the footer files it?

Q5 · Approved copy that would change (yes/no each): (a) header X facts “6-week install, then retainer” → “Scoped at the readout”, “Seven artifacts you own” → the layer's two assets; (b) nav 02.2 “Outbound engine build” → “Data pipeline & signal map”; (c) The Firm and Resources plate copy, incl. “Get in touch” → “Talk to the team”; (d) one quiet “Inside this layer →” link per open System ledger row on the homepage (today the homepage never reaches a capability page).

Q6 · Your published notes: fix 95% → 83% in the 17% note? The read times show 6/5/5 min but read in about 3/2/2 (also on the homepage letter and evidence door) — correct or keep? Byline “Rameez, founder” on each note?

Q7 · How you work: is the week on /about (Mon signal review … Thu kill review, Fri written note) how your engagements will run? Careers policies — no juniors, pay published with every role, remote-first and London-based?
